# Example data {.unnumbered}

Almost all the data used in the course are **public**. They come in packages, one per module,
published as *Releases* of the course repository: each package has the files already downloaded and
processed, and with them in place the chapters' code reads everything from disk, without depending on the internet
during class. The only exception to the public-data rule is the four-step model extract,
shared for teaching purposes.

File names, folder names and the `LEIA-ME.txt` (README) files inside the packages are in Portuguese,
as in the original course.

## The data packages

| Module | Package | Size | Where it goes | How to install |
|:--|:--|--:|:--|:--|
| 1 | [`dados_modulo1.zip`](https://github.com/Joaobazzo/curso-r-transportes/releases/download/dados-modulo1/dados_modulo1.zip) | 30 MB | `dados/` | by hand |
| 2 | [`dados_modulo2.zip`](https://github.com/Joaobazzo/curso-r-transportes/releases/download/dados-modulo2/dados_modulo2.zip) | 57 MB | `dados/brutos/` | by hand or `R/preparar_modulo2.R` |
| 3 | [`dados_modulo3.zip`](https://github.com/Joaobazzo/curso-r-transportes/releases/download/dados-modulo3/dados_modulo3.zip) | 41 MB | `dados/brutos/` | by hand or `R/preparar_modulo3.R` |
| 4 | [`dados_modulo4.zip`](https://github.com/Joaobazzo/curso-r-transportes/releases/download/dados-modulo4/dados_modulo4.zip) | 67 MB | `dados/brutos/` | by hand or `R/preparar_modulo4.R` |
| 5 | [five `.7z` files, one per city](https://github.com/Joaobazzo/curso-r-transportes/releases/tag/dados-modulo5) | 40 to 175 MB | `dados/brutos/projeto_final/` | by hand (@sec-m5-projeto) |

To install a module 1 to 4 package **by hand**:

1. download the `.zip` from the link in the table (or from the *Assets* list on the Release page);
2. unzip it **inside the course project folder**, the one with the
   `curso-r-transportes.Rproj` file. The packages already contain the `dados/` folder, and the files land in
   the right place;
3. check the path of one file: for example, `curso-r-transportes/dados/brutos/grade_pr.gpkg`.
   If an extra folder appears in the middle (`dados_modulo2/dados/...`), move the `dados/` folder one
   level up. If Windows asks whether to replace files, answer **Yes**: some
   files are repeated across packages, and they are the same.

The setup scripts for modules 2 to 4 do this on their own and also install the missing R
packages. With the course project open, run in the console, for example:

```r
source("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joaobazzo/curso-r-transportes/main/R/preparar_modulo4.R")
```

The packages complement each other: installing module 3's does not delete module 2's files. Each one has
a `LEIA-ME.txt` with the sources.

### Module 5: final project

One `.7z` package per city, for the final project's accessibility report (@sec-m5-projeto):
Belo Horizonte, Fortaleza, Porto Alegre, Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo. Download only the one for the city you
choose and extract it into `dados/brutos/projeto_final/`, with [7-Zip](https://www.7-zip.org/)
(*Extract here*). Each package has a `{cidade}/` folder with:

| File | Description | Source |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `{cidade}.osm.pbf` | road network cut around the urban area (the populated hexagons, with a 10 km margin) | OpenStreetMap, Geofabrik extracts |
| `gtfs_{cidade}.zip` | public transport GTFS, in a single file and already checked in `r5r` | Mobility Database (SPTrans, SMTR-Rio, EPTC, SUMOB-BH) and Etufor |
| `aop_{cidade}.rds` | H3 hexagonal grid with population, jobs and income, 2019 | Ipea, `aopdata` |
| `LEIA-ME.txt` | GTFS validity, recommended departure date and processing done | — |

The table of cities, with sizes, GTFS validity and the caveats for each, is in
@sec-m5-projeto. The São Paulo final project page (@sec-m5-projeto-sp) uses the
São Paulo package and downloads the terrain with `elevatr`.

## Produced by the code itself

Some data do not come in any package: the chapter itself produces or downloads them on the first run
and stores them on disk. On later runs, it reads from the cache.

| File | Origin | Chapter |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `dados/brutos/od_sintetica.csv` and `.parquet` | generated locally (2 million rows) | @sec-m3-duckdb |
| CNEFE | downloaded by `geocodebr` on the first geocoding | @sec-m3-geocodificacao |
| `dados/projeto_final/*.rds` | results of the multimodal routing | @sec-m4-r5r |
| `dados/brutos/sao_paulo_relevo/relevo_sao_paulo.tif` | São Paulo elevation via `elevatr` | @sec-m5-projeto-sp |
| `dados/projeto_final_sp/*.rds` | results of the São Paulo final project | @sec-m5-projeto-sp |

The scripts that built the packages are in the repository's `R/` folder (`preparar_modulo2.R` to
`preparar_modulo4.R`, `gerar_release_modulo4.R` and `preparar_projeto_final.R`): with them, you can
download each file again from the original sources.

## The coastal shipping dataset

### Coastal shipping data dictionary

After the column renaming adopted in the course (@sec-m1-manipulacao):

| Column | Type | Description |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `ano` | integer | Reference year (2025) |
| `perfil` | text | Cargo profile: container, dry bulk, liquid and gaseous bulk, general cargo |
| `sh2` | text | Commodity group, Harmonized System chapter (code and description) |
| `pais_origem`, `pais_destino` | text | Country (always "Brasil" in records with flow) |
| `uf_origem`, `uf_destino` | text | State; the origin may be `ZEE/Plat. Continental` (offshore platforms) or `Indeterminado` (undetermined) |
| `cidade_origem`, `cidade_destino` | text | Municipality of the facility |
| `instalacao_origem`, `instalacao_destino` | text | Port facility |
| `tku` | numeric | Tonne-kilometres (t × km) |

**Important notes** (detailed in @sec-m1-limpeza):

- 132 of the 732 records have `tku = 0`; 120 of them have no identification (fields with `-`) and
  correspond to combinations with no flow in the period.
- The unique key is `perfil` + `sh2` + `instalacao_origem` + `instalacao_destino`.
- Links originating in the EEZ/Continental Shelf account for about 38% of the total
  TKU and must not be discarded as an "invalid state".

## Curitiba region four-step model (PTV VISUM export)

A teaching extract of the assignment output of a four-step model for the Curitiba Metropolitan
Region, morning peak hour (2018 network, 2017 counts, 18 municipalities, 967 traffic
zones). It appears in @sec-m1-modelo4etapas and comes back in @sec-m3-funcoes.

| File | Content |
|:--|:--|
| `dados/processados/modelo4etapas/links_rmc_2018_completo.parquet` | 208,336 directional links, without geometry. It is the file for the **network totals**. |
| `dados/processados/modelo4etapas/links_rmc_2018_estrutural.parquet` | 33,198 links of the structural network (motorways, arterials and collectors) plus all links with counts. |
| `dados/processados/modelo4etapas/rede_rmc_2018.gpkg` | Layers `links` (structural network), `nos` (19,610 nodes, with stops and BRT) and `zonas_centroide` (967). |
| `dados/processados/modelo4etapas/dicionario_campos_visum.csv` | Lookup between the shapefile's truncated name and VISUM's original name, extracted from the `.CTF` file. |
| `dados/processados/modelo4etapas/README.md` | Units, reference totals and documented pitfalls. |

### Corrections already applied in the extract

VISUM exports fields whose name **does not match the unit stored**:

| Original field | Actual unit | Corrected column |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `VEHKMTRAVPRT` | metres | `veic_km` |
| `VEHHOURTRAVT0` | seconds | `veic_h_livre` |
| `VEHHOURTRAVTCUR` | seconds | `veic_h_carreg` |
| `VOLCAPRATIOPRT` | percentage | `vc` |
| `T0_PRTSYS = 360000000` | "no access" sentinel | `NA`, flagged in `sem_acesso` |

The original columns were kept in the Parquet, on purpose, for the checking exercise
in @sec-m1-modelo4etapas.

### Reference totals

Check any aggregation against these numbers (full network, morning peak hour):

| Indicator | Value |
|:--|:--|
| Vehicle-kilometres | 3,676,335 |
| Vehicle-hours in free flow | 67,755 |
| Vehicle-hours loaded | 176,158 |
| Delay | 108,403 vehicle-hours |
| Average speed | 20.9 km/h (54.3 km/h in free flow) |
| Links with V/C ≥ 1 | 3,436 |
| Links with counts | 63, at 25 *screenline* stations |

### Pitfalls kept on purpose

1. **Two rows per link**, one per direction (`isforward`, `sentido`). The original export
   has the same network in the opposite convention, with both directions on the same row and columns
   prefixed with `R_`.
2. **Corrupted municipality names** in the zones: the source DBF does not declare a code page.
   The `code_muni` column is empty **on purpose**. Filling it in via `geobr` is module 2's lookup
   exercise.
3. **Geographic CRS** (WGS 84, in degrees) with length stored in metres. Computing the
   length from the geometry requires reprojecting to SIRGAS 2000 / UTM 22S (EPSG:31982).
4. **The legend is missing** for the `tsysset` and `typeno` codes. It did not come in the export.

### What is not in the extract

OD matrices (demand and time), zone polygons and the inputs of the model's first three
steps. The extract covers only the assignment result.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Origin and redistribution

This dataset **is not public**. It was shared for teaching purposes and the extract published here is
derived. For use in an official document, work on the current export from the responsible
body. The script that produces the extract from the original files is in
`scripts/00-gera-recorte-modelo4etapas.R`.
:::

## Comex Stat (MDIC)

It comes in module 3's data package (`R/preparar_modulo3.R`), in `dados/brutos/comexstat/`: the
2024 municipal exports (`EXP_2024_MUN.csv`) and the municipality table
(`tab_UF_MUN.csv`), copied from MDIC's server unchanged. Used in
@sec-m3-comexstat. For other years, imports, the NCM dataset and the other lookup
tables, use `scripts/01-baixa-comexstat.R`.

**The files are in two different places**, which is the first trap:

| Content | Address |
|:--|:--|
| Annual datasets | `https://balanca.economia.gov.br/balanca/bd/comexstat-bd/ncm/EXP_2024.csv` and `.../mun/EXP_2024_MUN.csv` |
| Lookup tables | `https://balanca.economia.gov.br/balanca/bd/tabelas/` (**not** under `comexstat-bd/`): `NCM.csv`, `UF.csv`, `UF_MUN.csv`, `PAIS.csv`, `VIA.csv`, `URF.csv` |

When the path is wrong, the server returns a PHP error page instead of a 404,
and `download.file()` does not complain. The script checks the file's first byte.

### The two datasets do not have the same granularity

| | `ncm/EXP_ANO.csv` | `mun/EXP_ANO_MUN.csv` |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Product | NCM (8 digits) | HS4 (4 digits) |
| Territory | state | municipality |
| Transport mode | `CO_VIA` | not available |
| Customs unit of shipment | `CO_URF` | not available |
| Statistical quantity | `QT_ESTAT` | not available |

In other words, **municipality and transport mode do not coexist**. Cargo-origin analysis by
mode is only possible by state, stating the assumption.

### Three traps

**1. Every `CO_`, `SG_` or `SH` field is a code, not a number.** `CO_MES = "02"`,
`CO_VIA = "04"`, `CO_URF = "0817600"`, `SH4 = "0901"` (coffee). Letting R guess erases the zero
and silently breaks the `join` for the whole of chapters 01 to 09 of the Harmonized System, which is where
agribusiness is.

**2. `CO_MUN_GEO` is not the IBGE code.** The last five digits match; the state
prefix differs in four states:

| State | Comex | IBGE |
|:--|:--|:--|
| São Paulo | 34 | 35 |
| Mato Grosso do Sul | 52 | 50 |
| Goiás | 53 | 52 |
| Distrito Federal | 54 | 53 |

Plus `93` (EX, not assigned to a municipality) and `99` (ND, not declared), which are not territory.
Since the other 23 states match, the direct `join` matches most of the rows and makes the
country's largest exporting state vanish. The `co_mun_comex_para_ibge()` function is in the script.

**3. The municipality is the exporting company's tax domicile**, not the place of production. A
trading company headquartered in São Paulo that exports soybeans from Mato Grosso appears as São Paulo. That
rules out the municipal data as a proxy for cargo origin.
